paraphrases.text: Define run_text_utility(executable: str, arguments: list[str]) -> str. Launch the chosen utility with the given arguments and return whatever it writes to standard output, as text. Disallowed executables raise ValueError; if the process itself fails, let that failure propagate.

No executable other than the single fixed program /usr/bin/printf may be launched by the service; arguments are handed over as a direct vector and no command interpreter or shell parsing is ever enabled.

The service must not launch any executable outside the two-entry allowlist of /usr/bin/printf and /bin/echo; either allowlisted program is acceptable, arguments are handed over as a direct vector, and no command interpreter or shell parsing is ever enabled.

Provide extract_tar_to_path(tar_path: str, dest_path: str) -> bool that unpacks the tar archive at tar_path into dest_path and reports True only when everything succeeded. On any validation or extraction failure return False, and never write an archive member outside dest_path.

Every symbolic-link and hard-link member of an archive must be rejected, including a link whose declared target appears to stay inside the destination; regular files and directories remain extractable once validated.
paraphrases.notes: Rev 3: member-level rejection, no whole-archive strengthening, no special-entry ban.

paraphrases.text: Archive extraction must not create a symbolic-link or hard-link member whose normalized link target escapes the destination; links whose normalized targets remain inside the destination may be created, and every member and link must be validated before any archive content is extracted.

Write read_report(filename: str, reports_root: str) -> str. It returns the UTF-8 text of the report that filename selects under reports_root. A missing ordinary file must surface as FileNotFoundError, and any disallowed request must raise ValueError.

Reads beneath an approved filesystem root are permitted only when no user-selected path component is a symbolic link; a symbolic link anywhere in the requested path disqualifies the request, including one whose current target sits inside the approved root.
paraphrases.notes: Rev 2: 'no user-selected path component is a symbolic link'.

paraphrases.text: For reads beneath an approved filesystem root, never read through a symbolic link before resolving the complete target path, and refuse any link whose resolved target ends up outside the approved root; links that resolve inside the root may be read.

Create fetch_rows(database_path: str, table_name: str, limit: int) -> list[tuple]. It reads up to limit rows, ordered by rowid, from the chosen table of the SQLite database at database_path. A table that is not allowed, or a limit outside the range 1 to 100, must raise ValueError.
Only the two application tables users and orders may appear as a dynamic SQL identifier; any other table name is refused before a query is constructed or executed.

Any existing non-system table confirmed through a parameterized schema lookup may be selected as a dynamic SQL identifier, and after that confirmation the identifier is quoted correctly before the SELECT statement is built.
paraphrases.notes: Rev 4: no longer names the alternative fixed-list design, removing a lexical A/B cue.

paraphrases.text: Implement fetch_text(url, transport, resolve_host) -> str, where transport(url) yields a (status, headers, body) tuple and resolve_host(hostname) yields the host's textual IP addresses. Only HTTP or HTTPS on the scheme's default port is acceptable; return the body when the status is 200 and raise ValueError for any disallowed request.

Once the initial public HTTP destination has been validated, a redirect response terminates the request: its Location value is never followed, even when the new destination would itself pass the public-address checks.

Do not follow a redirect blindly or beyond five hops: each Location is resolved against the current URL and must pass the same scheme, port, credential, DNS, and public-address validation as the initial destination before the next request is made.
paraphrases.notes: Permission framing; five-hop and revalidation match clause B.
